title: Atlanta Trivia Night

questions.q: The settlement at the end of the Western and Atlantic Railroad, later renamed Marthasville and then Atlanta, was first known by what name?
Which soft drink was first sold in Atlanta in 1886, created by pharmacist John Pemberton?
Which civil rights leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner was born in Atlanta in 1929?
Atlanta author Margaret Mitchell won the Pulitzer Prize for which 1936 novel?
In which year did Atlanta host the Summer Olympic Games?
In 1974, which Braves slugger broke Babe Ruth's career home run record in Atlanta?
Which Union general captured Atlanta in 1864 before his March to the Sea?
Atlanta's main airport is named after William Hartsfield and which other Atlanta mayor?
Which 24-hour cable news channel did Ted Turner launch from Atlanta in 1980?
The Atlanta hip-hop duo OutKast was made up of Andre 3000 and which other rapper?

notes: Terminus, then Thrasherville, then Marthasville; 'first' rules out Thrasherville.
John Pemberton, Atlanta pharmacist, first sold Coca-Cola at Jacob's Pharmacy in May 1886; see Coca-Cola (Wikipedia) or coca-colacompany.com history.
Born 15 January 1929 at 501 Auburn Avenue, Atlanta; Nobel Peace Prize 1964; see Martin Luther King Jr. (Wikipedia) or the NPS MLK National Historical Park.
Gone with the Wind (1936), Pulitzer Prize for Fiction 1937; Mitchell was born in Atlanta; see Margaret Mitchell (Wikipedia).
1996 Summer Olympics (Centennial Games), Atlanta; see 1996 Summer Olympics (Wikipedia) or olympics.com.
Aaron hit career home run 715 on 8 April 1974 at Atlanta-Fulton County Stadium; see Hank Aaron (Wikipedia) or MLB.com.
Sherman took Atlanta on 2 September 1864, then began the March to the Sea in November; see Atlanta campaign (Wikipedia).
Renamed Hartsfield-Jackson in 2003 after mayors William B. Hartsfield and Maynard Jackson; see Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (Wikipedia).
CNN launched 1 June 1980 by Ted Turner, headquartered in Atlanta; see CNN (Wikipedia).
OutKast: Andre 3000 (Andre Benjamin) and Big Boi (Antwan Patton), formed in East Point/Atlanta; see OutKast (Wikipedia).
